details:
Abandoned, Not Forgotten: Off-World Monuments of Human Curiosity

Challenge: Challenge 1 — Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars

Team Name: HelloSpace!

Created by: Azhar Ahmed

Target Audience: School-age & casual space enthusiasts (Ages 10–16)

Introduction

Hello! My name is Azhar Ahmed, and I represent Team HelloSpace! for Challenge 1: Abandoned but not Forgotten.

Growing up fascinated by space exploration, I realized that while everyone celebrates active rovers and newly launched rockets, the pioneering machines that made today's discoveries possible often fade into dense technical tables. For this challenge, I wanted to build something that bridges aerospace engineering with emotional storytelling—an interactive digital museum where school-age space enthusiasts can meet NASA's retired landers, rovers, and deep-space probes face-to-face and hear their stories in their own words.

Project Summary

Abandoned, Not Forgotten is an interactive, story-driven web experience that brings thirteen legendary NASA spacecraft, rovers, and scientific instruments left on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space back to life. By combining verified telemetry from the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) with first-person hardware narratives, an interactive Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) surface map, synthesized deep-space radio pings, and a Cadet Historian verification pass, the project turns raw space history into an engaging hands-on adventure.

The Problem & Our Solution

  • The Problem: Over the last 60+ years, NASA has left dozens of remarkable robotic explorers across the solar system. Today, young learners mostly hear about ongoing missions, while historical spacecraft are buried inside complex catalogs and textbooks that lack narrative spark.
  • Our Solution: Team HelloSpace! transformed NSSDCA mission data into an accessible, browser-based experience designed specifically for ages 10–16. Instead of listing dry specifications, each piece of hardware speaks in the first person—explaining why it was built, how it survived extreme off-world environments, and what groundbreaking science it unlocked for humanity.

Key Features & Interactive Experience

1. Interactive Surface Beacon Map & LRO Lunar Workstation

  • Three Celestial Sectors: Explorers can switch seamlessly between The Moon, Mars, and Deep Space & Asteroids to click pulsing monument beacons plotted at their authentic resting coordinates.
  • Realistic Lunar Topographic Sector: Built with NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) nearside imagery, procedural regolith relief shading, Sector Zoom presets (1x Disk, East Maria, West Storms), an interactive Solar Terminator Phase Slider to sweep day/night shadows across craters and mare basins, and live Selenographic Lat/Lon & LOLA Elevation cursor readouts.
  • Live Light-Time Signal Delay Bar: Demonstrates the real physics of deep-space communication ($c = 299,792\text{ km/s}$), visualizing the delay from 1.28 seconds (Moon) to 12 minutes 40 seconds (Mars) and 19+ hours (Pioneer 10).

2. First-Person Artifact Logs & Dual Media Viewer (13 Monuments)

  • Authentic Voice of the Hardware: Covers 13 iconic artifacts—including Apollo 11's Eagle Descent Stage, Apollo 15's LRV-1, ALSEP Laser Retroreflectors, Surveyor 3, Sojourner, Opportunity, Viking 1, InSight, Ingenuity, NEAR Shoemaker, Dawn, Pioneer 10, and Kepler.
  • Archival Photo / Blueprint SVG Toggle: Students can switch between real NASA mission photography and custom-crafted aerospace vector schematics inside every artifact reader.

3. Sensory Telemetry Audio & Voice Narration

  • Ping Monument Beacon: Powered by the Web Audio API, each monument features a synthesized radio carrier ping paired with a real-time HTML5 Canvas oscilloscope.
  • Listen to Log: Integrated Web Speech API narration reads each spacecraft's story aloud, making the platform accessible and engaging like an interactive space podcast.

4. Cadet Field Verification Quiz & Downloadable Credential

  • Students test what they learned in a 5-question mission briefing to unlock and download a personalized Junior Off-World Historian Credential boarding pass as a high-resolution PNG or printable certificate.

Technical Stack & Data Accuracy

  • Data Sources: Coordinates, NSSDCA IDs, mission timelines, and scientific findings verified through the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) and NASA/JPL public-domain imagery.
  • Technology: Built as a zero-dependency, single-file responsive web application using HTML5, Tailwind CSS, HTML5 Canvas, interactive SVG, Web Audio API, and Web Speech API.
